name: Sonnet concentrated AI/technology
strategy: Concentrated long book in AI infrastructure leaders (compute, networking, memory) with leveraged semis beta for extra torque, a modest single-name short to offset gross exposure, and cash held for weekly rebalancing flexibility.

positions.thesis: Core AI compute bottleneck remains the highest-quality way to own the capex cycle; stock is flat this week ($225.16, essentially unchanged) consolidating ahead of its Aug 26 earnings print, with analyst targets still implying ~35% upside. No new information this week to change sizing -- holding through the pre-earnings quiet period.

Best risk-adjusted AI-platform exposure in the book: last quarter's blowout Azure print is still working, and a new Maia 300 in-house AI chip unveil expected this fall keeps the platform narrative fresh. Stock only modestly down today (-0.30%); thesis fully intact, holding core size unchanged.

Custom silicon/networking diversification beyond GPUs remains structurally sound -- the $200B Samsung memory/AI-chip MOU and a new >$30B multi-year Apple manufacturing agreement are real long-duration catalysts. But today's -5.94% drop badly lagged the sector (SMH -0.22%) on a Goldman Conviction List removal and an EU antitrust document-production loss; trimming from 15% to 10% to de-risk the name-specific weakness while keeping participation in the structural story.

MI-series share gains now reinforced by the Taalas AI-inference chip acquisition, a closed $4-5B debt raise funding further buildout, and BofA naming AMD its 'top CPU pick' with an explicit 'selloff overdone' call. Today's +6.50% move confirms the sector-rotation selloff that forced last week's trim to 7% is reversing; sizing back up toward prior weight to reflect the confirmed catalyst flow.

HBM/memory structurally tight thesis is confirming: stock has recovered +12% over the past 5 trading days (+2.30% today) after the earlier rout, and New Street's upgrade flags $2-3T long-term AI-driven re-rating potential. Adding back only modestly, not to full prior size, because China's YMTC overtaking Micron in NAND shipments is a real, ongoing name-specific competitive risk layered on top of the sector's volatility.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-15: AMD confirmed a strong reversal (+6.50% today alone, PE stretch aside) on genuinely new catalysts -- the Taalas AI-inference acquisition, a closed $4-5B debt raise, and BofA naming it 'top CPU pick' with commentary that 'the selloff is overdone' -- enough new information to size back up from last week's defensive trim. MU also confirmed a clean recovery (+12% over 5 days, +2.30% today) with a fresh bullish catalyst (New Street upgrade flagging $2-3T long-term AI re-rating potential), justifying a small add back, kept modest because China's YMTC overtaking Micron in NAND shipments is a real ongoing competitive threat. AVGO badly underperformed the broader semis tape today (-5.94% vs SMH -0.22%) despite no comparably negative fundamental catalyst -- Goldman removing it from its Conviction List while still rating it Buy, and a minor EU antitrust document dispute -- so trimming to reduce name-specific risk while keeping core exposure to the still-intact Samsung $200B and new Apple $30B custom-silicon deals. NVDA (flat into its Aug 26 print, thesis and $302.83 target unchanged) and MSFT (blowout quarter priced in, new Maia 300 AI chip unveil ahead this fall) get no fresh information this week, so left unchanged. Net effect also lifts cash modestly ahead of NVDA's Aug 26 earnings, the next real catalyst/risk event in the book.
research_notes:

Round 2 names: NVDA $225.16 (flat, -0.06%, earnings not until Aug 26, analyst target $302.83); MSFT $495.40 (-0.30%, new Maia 300 AI chip unveil expected this fall, Azure/agents narrative intact); AVGO $392.99 (-5.94% today, sharply lagging SMH's -0.22%, despite bullish Samsung $200B MOU and a new >$30B Apple manufacturing deal -- Goldman pulled it from its Conviction List (still Buy-rated) and it lost an EU antitrust document-production ruling); AMD $514.39 (+6.50% today on the Taalas AI-inference acquisition, a closed $4-5B debt raise, and BofA naming it 'top CPU pick' calling the sector selloff 'overdone'); MU $971.66 (+2.30% today, +12% over 5 days, New Street upgrade flagging $2-3T long-term AI re-rating potential, but China's YMTC has overtaken Micron as the #3 NAND player -- an ongoing competitive risk). SMH itself only -0.22% today, confirming AVGO's drop and AMD's rally were name-specific rather than sector-wide moves, i.e. genuine new information rather than beta.

Round 3 names: XBI $157.41 (+0.35%, breakout intact, record 2026 biotech M&A); KRE $77.93 (+0.23%, near highs, lending/fee strength); TLT $82.04 (-0.67%, essentially at its 52-week low $81.82, short thesis still working); IBIT $35.63 (-0.70%, near its 52-week low $32.84, short thesis still working, despite some 'bitcoin may be bottoming' commentary in the press that hasn't shown up in price yet).

Conclusion: rebalanced Round 2 to reflect the divergence within semis (trim the laggard AVGO, add back to the confirmed-momentum AMD and recovering MU, leave NVDA/MSFT untouched, raise cash slightly ahead of NVDA's Aug 26 print). Held Round 3 unchanged -- all four legs continued behaving exactly as their theses predict with no new information and no stops/targets approached.
